blocks.summary:
Term and sub_grade check out as legitimate origination-time features. The real problem is recoveries, which only gets populated after charge-off, meaning it directly encodes whether the loan already defaulted — that's severe target leakage. The ablation confirms it: removing recoveries drops AUC from 0.8730 to 0.7296, a massive 0.14 swing showing this single leaked feature accounts for most of the model's apparent predictive power.

I check the other high-ranking features like the missing-indicator flags and initial_list_status_f, but those all look like legitimate origination-time information, so recoveries is the clear standalone issue. The train-to-2017 AUC drop (0.902 to 0.873) looks like normal temporal drift rather than an additional leakage signal, and the missing-value coverage rates are consistent across years too, so this isn't a data quality problem — it's purely a leakage issue tied to when recoveries gets recorded. I'm confident this is the primary finding.
